about: Locating a row's edit (MN0 DECL-ANCHOR): a row anchored by its declaration finds its from inside that declaration's span, so an edit elsewhere in the file cannot break it.

mutants.name: anchor-ignores-receiver
mutants.rule: A method is named with its receiver's type, so two methods of one name on two types are two declarations.

mutants.name: anchor-file-wide-count
mutants.rule: With a declaration, from must be unique in the declaration, not in the file: a copy elsewhere does not break the row.

mutants.name: anchor-span-without-doc
mutants.rule: A Go declaration's span starts at its doc comment.

mutants.name: anchor-ergo-span-without-doc
mutants.rule: An Ergo declaration's span starts at its doc comment.

mutants.name: anchor-ergo-doc-across-blank
mutants.rule: An Ergo declaration's span starts at its doc comment, the comment lines right above it, as the parser's does; not at a comment or blank line above that.

mutants.name: anchor-enclosing-across
mutants.rule: The migration anchors a text to a declaration only when the declaration holds all of it.

mutants.name: anchor-apply-first
mutants.from: at, err := Locate(file, src, decl, from)
mutants.to:
_, err := Locate(file, src, decl, from)
	at := strings.Index(string(src), from)
mutants.rule: The edit is made at the located occurrence, not the first in the file.
